title: Introduce kernel-affinity prefetch orchestrator and reproducible hotpath recorder
author: Ethan Cole
description: Motivation: reproduce and measure prefetch behavior deterministically across CI and local runs to triage kernel-affinity regressions affecting p95/p99 tails. This PR adds a lightweight prefetch orchestrator that deterministically schedules primer requests and a reproducible hotpath recorder that emits a compact seed+trace artifact usable by the benchmark harness to replay identical scheduling and kernel affinity sequences. Changes include a seedable scheduler, durable prefetch plan serialization, a deterministic randomizer for primer selection, and a compact binary trace schema with an optional JSON fallback. The goal is to enable: 1) stable perf baselines for nightly/regression suites, 2) root-cause analysis of kernel-affinity induced tail-latency spikes, 3) a reproducible on-demand replay mode that can be shipped to infra for postmortems. Compatibility: default behavior is opt-in for existing runners; no change to current nightly flows unless enable_prefetch_orchestrator=true in benchmark config. See linked Linear items for rollout plan and integration tests.

release_notes: Adds an opt-in deterministic prefetch orchestrator and a reproducible hotpath recorder for benchmark replaying and root-cause analysis. Nightly baselines can opt-in to produce seed+trace artifacts for reproducible tail investigations.
notes: Initial CI run failed due to platform-specific timer flakiness; rerun with linux-only integration and stabilized cleanup. Opt-in flag prevents user-facing behavior changes. The compact_trace.proto is intentionally minimal to keep artifacts small and fast to ship.
